title: Attested Accelerator Fallback and Warmstart Playbook
author: Marco Chen
content:
Summary
-------
This playbook documents the recommended architecture, operational runbook, and customer prerequisites for orchestrating hardware-accelerator fallback (e.g. GPU -> CPU, newer accelerator -> older accelerator) in private VPC and on‑prem Redwood deployments. It also defines warmstart (partial-model KV prefill) procedures to mitigate cold-start latency when fallback occurs or when nodes are brought online. The goal is to keep tenant SLOs intact while minimizing cost and preserving forensics and attestation evidence for regulated customers.

Audience
--------
- Field operators and SREs running private deployments
- Solutions engineers designing tenant-level resilience profiles
- Security/Compliance teams that need attestation and evidence chains during failover

Scope and assumptions
---------------------
- Applies to Redwood Private (VPC + on‑prem) customer deployments that use hardware accelerators (NVIDIA A100/H100, AMD MI, or equivalent) managed by our operator.
- Assumes control plane connectivity (or delegated control plane) for telemetry and rollout orchestration.
- Assumes operator has access to runtime attestation APIs and signed firmware/driver bundles.

Key concepts and terms
----------------------
- Accelerator fallback: transparent redirection of inference traffic from a primary accelerator class to an alternate execution path (different card class, CPU fallback, quantized variant).
- Warmstart: pre-populating model KV cache and prefix encoders to reduce first-request latency after model swap or node spin-up.
- Attestation: cryptographic verification of hardware, firmware, and runtime before allowing model keys or sensitive telemetry to be used on a node.

Design patterns
---------------
1) Hierarchical fallback with policy tiers
   - Preferred: same-architecture hot-swap (H100 -> H100 spare in same zone).
   - Secondary: cross-architecture quantized fallback (H100 16-bit -> H100 int8 or A100 int8).
   - Tertiary: CPU fallback with strict rate-limit and degraded SLO (for low-volume, non-interactive workloads).

2) Attestation gating and evidence preservation
   - Only nodes that pass hardware attestation and driver checksum validation may receive model artifacts or KMS-unwrapped keys.
   - All attestation events and key unwraps are logged to an append-only evidence stream retained per-customer for configurable retention windows.

3) Staged warmstart prefill
   - Reactive warmstart: when fallback is triggered, the operator enqueues prioritized prompt sets to prefill KV for the most common prefixes within 30–60 seconds.
   - Preemptive warmstart: when capacity forecasts predict an upcoming surge, the operator can prefill warm pools using synthetic prompt traces (customer-provided or anonymized patterns).

SLOs and degradations
----------------------
- Normal SLO: p50 < 70ms token, p95 < 350ms token for interactive tiers.
- Allowed degraded SLO on fallback: p50 < 150ms token, p95 < 1200ms token.
- Warmstart objective: reduce cold-start tail by 60–80% for the top 20 prompt prefixes within 90s after node readiness.

Configuration table (recommended defaults)
----------------------------------------
| Parameter | Default | Notes |
|---|---:|---|
| fallback.policy.tier_order | ["zone-hotspare","quantized-fanout","cpu-fallback"] | Operators may reorder per-customer SLAs |
| fallback.max_traffic_fraction | 0.25 | Max traffic to route to fallback pool during transient state |
| warmstart.prefill.top_k_prefixes | 20 | Prefill priority list per model per-tenant |
| warmstart.prefill.rate_limit | 50 qps | Aggregate prefill QPS to avoid denial of service on accelerator pools |
| attestation.timeout_seconds | 300 | Wait time for hardware attestation before aborting rollout |

Operational runbook: Typical failure -> recovery
------------------------------------------------
1) Detection
   - Trigger sources: scheduled maintenance, NVML/driver failure alert, elevated thermal events, control-plane node offline, or operator-initiated drain.
   - Alerting threshold: >1% error rate increase or 10% p95 latency regression per model-route triggers incident.

2) Immediate mitigation (automated)
   - Step A: Shift 10–25% of new traffic to warm spare pool in same zone (circuit-breaker).
   - Step B: If spare capacity unavailable, trigger quantized-fanout and activate preconfigured quantized model variants.
   - Step C: Start warmstart prefill for top_k_prefixes for affected model versions.

3) Attestation validation
   - Ensure nodes targeted for fallback present valid TPM/SE attestation response. CLI check: redwoodctl node attest --node <id> --expect OK
   - If attestation fails, mark node quarantined and route traffic around it; capture evidence bundle for compliance.

4) Capacity stabilization
   - Monitor token-level cost and latency. If p95 remains above degraded threshold for >5 minutes, perform controlled widening of fallback to adjacent zone (with customer consent if indicated by SLA).

5) Recovery and rollback
   - If primary hardware recovers, perform staged model rehydration and traffic ramp (10% -> 25% -> 50% -> 100%) with warmstart prefills at each step.
   - If fallback variant causes quality regressions (detected by eval callbacks), automatically traffic-shift back to the last-known-good model variant and open a regression incident.

Automation examples (redwoodctl snippets)
----------------------------------------
- Trigger tolerant fallback (operator):
  redwoodctl fallback create --tenant <tenant-id> --model <model-id> --policy quantized-fanout --max-fraction 0.2

- Start warmstart prefill for a model shard:
  redwoodctl warmstart prefill --model <model-id> --tenant <tenant-id> --prefix-file /tmp/top20-prefixes.txt --rate 30

- Verify attestation evidence and fetch bundle:
  redwoodctl node attest --node <node-id> --fetch-evidence /tmp/evidence-<node-id>.tar.gz

Customer prerequisites checklist
-------------------------------
1) Network
   - Control-plane endpoints reachable from nodes (HTTPS egress) or pre-approved delegated-control-plane arrangement.
   - TLS inspection disabled for KMS endpoints or appropriate certs installed.

2) Key management
   - Customer KMS/HSM configured with wrap/unwrap roles for Redwood operator key vendor.
   - Attestation CA chain accepted by customer operator image.

3) Workload profile and prefix corpus (recommended)
   - Customer provides top 100 prompt prefixes and a synthetic load profile or consents to Redwood synthetic trace usage for warmstart prefill.

4) SLA & policy contract
   - Must specify allowed fallback tiers and whether cross-zone fallback is permitted.

Testing and validation matrix
-----------------------------
- Smoke tests (pre-deploy):
  1) Attestation simulation: run with attestation-mock to ensure node rejects tampered images.
  2) Prefill throughput test: verify warmstart prefill at configured rate without node OOM.
- Chaos tests (periodic):
  1) Simulate accelerator removal and verify fallback completes within 90s and SLOs remain within degraded bounds.
  2) Introduce driver checksum mismatch to confirm quarantine and evidence bundling.

Telemetry and observability requirements
--------------------------------------
- Required metrics: fallback.activation.count, warmstart.prefill.latency, attestation.status.count, model.quality.regression.alerts.
- Logs: append-only evidence stream (customer-scoped), node driver checksums, KMS unwrap audit.
- Dashboards: per-tenant fallback heatmap, KV cache hit-rate, cold-start tail latency.

Security and compliance notes
-----------------------------
- Do not release unwrapped model keys to nodes until attestation passes.
- Evidence bundles must be signed and stored in the customer evidence bucket for at least the retention period required by the contract.

Operational responsibilities and ownership
----------------------------------------
- Operator: Redwood Field Ops — responsible for orchestrating fallback, running warmstart jobs, and evidence collection.
- Customer: Infrastructure / Security team — ensure KMS policies, network egress, and accept fallback policy.
- Escalation: Pager: field-sre@redwood.company -> oncall-sre -> eng-runtime-owner.

Rollout checklist for new customers
-----------------------------------
1) Validate attestation root chain and KMS handshake in staging.
2) Run a controlled failover simulation with customer-supplied prompt corpus.
3) Approve fallback policy tiers and thresholds in the onboarding contract.
4) Schedule a runbook dry-run with Field Ops and Customer NOC.

Related pages and references
---------------------------
- See: /confluence/eng-private-deployments/reference-architectures/gpu-topology-tenant-affinity-and-fallback-reference-2026
- See: /confluence/eng-private-deployments/day-2-ops/cold-start-latency-mitigation-for-private-deploys-2026

Appendix: common troubleshooting commands
----------------------------------------
- List current fallback policies: redwoodctl fallback list --tenant <tenant-id>
- Inspect warmstart queue: redwoodctl warmstart queue --status pending | running
- Force node quarantine: redwoodctl node quarantine --node <node-id> --reason "driver-mismatch"
